Package hadur2.core.policy

Class MirrorDetector

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.policy.MirrorDetector
public final class MirrorDetector extends Object
MIR-1: recognising a robot that moves as a mirror image of us.

Some simple robots (the RoboRumble's stelo.MirrorNano and MirrorMicro among them) drive, every tick, toward the reflection of our position through the battlefield's centre. Against them Hadur's gun hit about 8% on the 3.4 bench: their path follows ours, which none of the gun's features describe. A robot that mirrors us is, though, exactly predictable from our own path, which Hadur decides.

Each scan, the detector is given the enemy's position and our own position over the last MAX_LAG ticks. For each lag it keeps a running error: how far the enemy is from the reflection of where we were that many ticks ago, an exponential average with weight ALPHA. The response is active once the best of those errors has stayed under ON_ERROR px for ON_SCANS scans running (PRIMED_SCANS once a mirror has been confirmed this battle), and clears as soon as it goes over OFF_ERROR.

The run is long because two surfers orbiting each other about a point near the centre look like a mirror for a while: on the top-19 benches the longest such run under 30 px was 80 scans, while MirrorNano's and MirrorMicro's shortest was 152 (they mirror from the first tick to the last). Scans while either robot has MIN_ENERGY energy or less do not extend the run (a scan off the reflection still breaks it): two nearly disabled robots crawling about stayed at each other's reflection for 335 scans in one round against Neuromancer. Only the reflection through the centre is checked: the axis mirrors, which no RoboRumble robot is known to use, matched surfers far more often.

Plain values in, plain values out: positions in px, the field's size, no engine types (DIAL-2). newRound() forgets the run; the errors and the confirmation are kept, since a mirror bot mirrors in every round.
